# Data processing rules -
1. Identify and handle missing values
2. Data Formatting
3. Data Normalization (centering / scaling)
4. Data Binning
5. Turning Categorical to numerical variables

# Deal with missing data
1. Drop the missing values
    a. drop the variable
    b. drop the data entry
2. Replace the missing values
    a. replace it with an average (of similar datapoints)
    b. replace it by frequency
    c. replace it based on other functions
3. Leave as it is

# How to drop missing values -
df.dropna() // axis = 0 (for entire row), axis = 1 (for entire column)
df.dropna(subset=["price"], axis=0, inplace = True)

# How to replace missing values -
df.replace(missing_value, new_value)
mean = df["normalized-losses"].mean()
df["normalized-losses"].replace(np.nan, mean)

# Data Formatting -
df ["city-mpg"] = 235 / df["city-mpg"]
df.rename(columns = {"city-mpg": "city-L/100km"}, inplace = True)

df["price"] = df["price"].astype("int") // convert data types

# Data Normalization
1. Simple Feature Scaling
df["length"] = df["length"] / df["length"].max()

2. Min-max
df["length"] = (df["length"] - df["length"].min()) / (df["length"].max() - df["length"].min())

3. Z-score
df["length"] = (df["length"] - df["length"].mean()) / df["length"].std()

# Binning
bins = np.linspace(min(df["price"]), max(df["price"]), 4)
group_names = ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
df["price-binned"] = pd.cut(df["price"], bins, lables=group_names, include_lowest = True)

# Turning Categorical to numerical variables
pd.get_dummies(df["fuel"])
